headline: Glen Canyon Entrance and Navajo Nation Permits
reservation: Entry requires a National Park Service pass for Glen Canyon NRA. Separate guided tour permits are mandatory for Antelope Canyon land access via Navajo Parks and Recreation; these often sell out months in advance. Water levels affect boat ramp availability; check the official NPS 'Changing Lake Levels' page.

days.title: Canyon Rims and River Curves

stops.name: Horseshoe Bend
stops.detail: Walk the 1.5-mile round-trip path to see the Colorado River's 270-degree curve from the rim.

stops.name: Glen Canyon Dam Overlook
stops.detail: Descend the rock-hewn steps for a perspective on the massive concrete structure and the river below.

days.note: Horseshoe Bend has no shade; avoid walking between 11 AM and 4 PM in summer.

days.title: Sandstone Walls by Water
days.start: Suggested: 7 AM from Antelope Point Launch

stops.name: Antelope Canyon (Water Access)
stops.detail: Paddle into the narrow sandstone slots reachable only by boat from the lake.

stops.name: Wahweap Overlook
stops.detail: Drive to this high point for a panoramic sunset view across the Utah border.

days.note: Morning wind is typically calmer; afternoon gusts can create hazardous chop on open water.

days.title: Navajo Sandstone and Hidden Geology

stops.name: Carl Hayden Visitor Center
stops.detail: View the dam interior (if tours available) and explore geological exhibits of the Colorado Plateau.

stops.name: Lone Rock Beach
stops.detail: Visit the shoreline in the Utah section for an expansive view of the iconic monolithic rock.

days.note: Vehicle access to Lone Rock shoreline depends on sand depth; check current clearance advice at the gate.

intel.title: Horseshoe Bend Fee
intel.text: The Horseshoe Bend parking lot is managed by the City of Page and requires a separate fee not covered by the America the Beautiful pass. Arrive before 8 AM to avoid the longest queues.

intel.title: Remote Dead Zones
intel.text: Signal is strong in Page but disappears immediately upon entering side canyons or traveling north on Highway 89. Use offline navigation for all lake access points.

intel.title: Page Service Hub
intel.text: Page is the only major fuel and grocery stop for 60 miles in any direction. Fill tanks before heading toward Big Water or Bullfrog.

intel.title: Arizona Time Zone
intel.text: Page, AZ stays on Mountain Standard Time year-round, while the nearby Navajo Nation and Utah follow Daylight Saving. Double-check tour times against your phone's auto-setting.

intel.title: Changing Ramps
intel.text: Low water levels frequently close the Wahweap and Antelope Point ramps to motorized vessels. Check the NPS 'Current Conditions' page daily for launch status.

plan.arrival: Fly into Page Municipal Airport (PGA); pick up your rental car and stock up on at least one gallon of water per person per day before heading to the marina.
plan.vehicle: A standard car works for Page sights; a 4WD is strongly suggested if you plan to access primitive shoreline areas like Lone Rock.
plan.goldenHour: Wahweap Overlook provides a 360-degree vista of the lake and white mesas, ideal for sunset photography.
